APPENDIX 8
OUR MATERIAL WORLD
FAQ: Well, to be honest, I just want all this stuff 
because … I want it! Is that so bad?
FAQ: Honestly, I don’t really care that much about my 
unique mission in this world. I just daven because I need 
stuff from Hashem. Is that so bad?
In the fifth chapter of
describes the ideal approach a person should take to running their lives, based on the Mishnah: “
— Everything you do should be for the sake of Heaven.” In theory, everything we do or say, everything we buy, and how we spend every minute of the day should all be based on what will maximize our
. In theory, why would we want something that will not help us in serving Hashem and help us in fulfilling our mission? What purpose would it serve? But the

himself says that this is a very high level of running one’s life, which is reached only by a select few and only after many years of work. But it is important to understand the concept and to have something to aim for.We should put thought into why we want stuff and why we spend money on things. Obviously, we can’t maximize our service of Hashem if we’re tired, hungry, cranky, tense, and irritable. So we do need some stuff to solve those issues — each in our own way and on our own level. But even for “normal” people, acquiring things just out of jealousy or to make others jealous of us is not healthy. And certainly, to use our material things to create a false sense of self is not going to help us grow.So to sum up, it is understandable that at a certain point in our lives we just “want stuff because I want it,” and no, that’s not so bad. But at least during our
to Hashem we should have a sense of what we are aspiring to.
